newsitem.title: UK: Underwater juggling, red noses as comics aid Africa.
newsitem.headline: Underwater juggling, red noses as comics aid Africa.

text.p: Britain broke out in a rash of false red noses and bizarre behaviour on Friday as comedians and celebrities led a drive to raise millions for the poor and disadvantaged at home and in Africa.

A scuba-diver planned to juggle underwater in a swimming pool in Chelmsford, southeast England, a London busdriver dressed as a woman for the day and a couple from Staffordshire, central England, planned to get married wearing red noses.
Sales of red noses are a key money spinner for the Comic Relief charity, which has raised 112 million pounds ($180 million) for the poor in Britain and Africa since it began in 1986.
More than 16 million of the noses, which are changed each time the fundraising day is held and include big versions for cars as well as people, have been sold.
This year around 200 red noses were shipped out to the Falkland Islands, Britain's colony in the South Atlantic, where residents have pledged a series of money-raising ideas.

Comedians, media personalities and pop stars take part in a live six-hour comedy festival on television on Friday night to boost donations to the charity, which began as an annual project but is now held every two years to prevent donor burnout.
One third of the money raised goes to British charities and the rest to projects in Africa. ($1=.6228 Pound)
